author: visegrad24
text:
BREAKING:

Swedish authorities are now investigating a second Somali politician’s campaign for election fraud.

Running for the far-left Left Party, Ahmed Abas Omar, is on track to win a municipal council seat in Borlänge through a surprisingly large number of personal votes for someone on the 6th place on the party’s electoral list.

With 28 of 29 districts counted he has 343 personal votes, far ahead of first-name candidate Emelie Larsson (147). 

Omar’s case is now also part of a police investigation into suspected election fraud run by the National Anti-Corruption Unit. 

The case concerns improper influence on voting. 

An anonymous report alleges that voters from migrant areas were bused to early voting and given pre-marked ballots. 

Omar and fellow Somali Left Party politician Mohamed Abdukardir Ali appear in image material in the investigation. 

Ali, who campaigned with Omar, won the party’s only seat in Dalarna for the Swedish Parliament, via more than 600 personal votes.

No one has yet been formally notified as a suspect.

Omar previously featured in local media articles  as chair of a community association accused of membership irregularities. 

When Swedish journalist approached him in front of his apartment yesterday morning, he first claimed that they had mistaken him for someone else and that his name wasn’t even Omar.

When he returned to his apartment in the evening and it turned out that the journalists were still there, he confirmed his identity, saying he was glad about receiving so many votes and referred further questions to the party’s press office.
